SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS "orders.n"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
), _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(AVG(customers.credit) AS DOUBLE) AS "customers.credit_avg"
  FROM customers AS customers
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
), _cm_orders__customers__credit_count AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(customers.credit) AS "customers.credit_count"
  FROM customers AS customers
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
)
SELECT
  _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg."customers.credit_avg" AS "orders.avg_credit",
  _base."orders.n",
  COALESCE(_cm_orders__customers__credit_count."customers.credit_count", 0) AS "orders.nc"
FROM _base
CROSS JOIN _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg
CROSS JOIN _cm_orders__customers__credit_count
LIMIT 21

WITH __slayer_stage_s1 AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."orders.id" AS "id",
    _stage_inner."orders.customers.credit" AS "customers__credit"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      orders.id AS "orders.id",
      customers.credit AS "orders.customers.credit"
    FROM orders AS orders
    LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
      ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
    WHERE
      NOT customers.id IS NULL
    GROUP BY
      orders.id,
      customers.credit
  ) AS _stage_inner
)
SELECT
  CAST(AVG(s1.customers__credit) AS DOUBLE) AS "s1.avg_credit",
  COUNT(*) AS "s1.n",
  COUNT(s1.customers__credit) AS "s1.nc"
FROM __slayer_stage_s1 AS s1
LIMIT 21

args.message: Weighting each order once, the average credit limit of the ordering customer is about 540.60. This covers the 5,010 orders whose customer_id matches a customer record. The other 6 orders have no matching customer and are left out. For comparison, if each customer counted once instead, the average would be about 553.61.
